coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: About 140,254 paid domestic workers (EHPM 2023) but ISSS affiliation is a voluntary regime (never above ~2,500 contributors); no mandatory duty, so little pull. Nothing new beyond ISSS/AFP payroll being covered by K06.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No national register or scrap-dealer law found; only a municipal (San Salvador Centro) enforcement case on a metal recycler. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No El Salvador pawnshop or second-hand register found (only a 2019 UES thesis on tax treatment). Whether AML duties apply is unverified (relates to K01).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Same search as 3: nothing specific to El Salvador found. AML status unverified (K01 adjacent).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler register or law found. Only the 2025 used-vehicle import rule (model year 2017 or newer), which is not a dismantler duty.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Brand (fierro) registration with MAG valid 5 years, via SIMPLE.SV, ownership transfer $33.90; New World screwworm emergency since Dec 2024 with inspection points at livestock markets (2,973 cases to June 2025). Movement-guide rules not confirmed. Weak candidate C5.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Municipal rastros inspect carcasses in practice; MAG proposed (Apr 2026) a reform naming MAG as certifier of meat, dairy and honey establishments, still in committee. No butcher duty confirmed. Candidate C9 (weak).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Beekeepers must be MAG-registered with a Código Único de Apicultor and follow RTS 65.03.01:14 for export honey; ~2,467 registered but only 200-350 active exporters; sector in crisis (Infobae May 2026). Candidate C8 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Clinics are authorised by the CSSP with a JVPMV favourable report (95% critical, 75% major criteria) and a regente who keeps the controlled-products book; annual solvency to the JVPMV. Candidate C7 (weak).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Ley General de Recursos Hídricos (2022): drillers and well users had to legalise with ASA, exploration permit up to 1 year (art. 98), well-registration form. Driller-side candidate C4, related to K03.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Ley Especial de Recolección, Aprovechamiento y Disposición Final de Residuos (DL 186, Dec 2024) created ANDRES; MARN fined or closed an unlicensed septic operator in 2023; hazardous-transport permit needs a MARN form plus fire-brigade certificates. No private hauler register found. Candidate C10 (unverified).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Decreto 254 mentions accredited experts for steam generators and pressure equipment, but no periodic inspection or certification regime found for lifts, boilers or pressure vessels. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03. ASA authorises juntas de agua inscription and use.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Dealers need a MAG-authorised establishment certificate and, under a 2004 decree, a sales control book recording buyer name, DUI, signature and intended use; aerial application rules from 2011. Candidate C6.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: MTPS Departamento Nacional de Empleo oversees private placement agencies (2017 UES thesis only); no current register or reporting rule found. Candidate C11 (unverified).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Ley General de Cementerios (DL 320) covers municipal, private and mixed cemeteries; municipalities must inspect every 6 months and some (Soyapango 2017) have ordinances for private cemeteries and funeral homes. No national register or 2025 change found. Candidate C12 (weak).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ley de Agentes Extranjeros in force 7 Jun 2025: RAEX registration within 90 days, 30% tax on foreign funds; many NGOs have closed. Annual audited financial statements are due to the Registro by end of April under the associations law; a fee/church-accounting bill stalled in the plenary in 2023 (status unknown). Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: New mandatory RTV for cargo (resolution DGTC-JDAA-UTTC-003/2026): cabezales from 8 Aug 2026 (annual), trailers (every 2 years), all tipper trucks from 5 Oct 2026; RTV is required for the circulation-card renewal; only 12 authorised workshops for 158,402 cargo units. Mototaxi permits not issued since 2010. Buses covered by K11. Candidate C2 and C3.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Vendors: San Salvador Centro special 2-year regime (Diario Oficial 1 Jul 2026) for ~250 evicted vendors, with municipal paperwork; permits are municipal and fragmented. Money changers not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: only 14 authorised vs up to 100 unauthorised; VMT requires cameras and exam software. Early-childhood centres need municipal site rating, MINSAL sanitary permit, fire-brigade certificate and MINEDUCYT accreditation. Tattoo studios, hunting and small food producers not searched. Candidates C13 and C14 (weak).

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Stations must report each price change to DGEHM (inspectors check; DGEHM asks managers to report by WhatsApp), and DGEHM checks volume, quality and safety; pump calibration must be done by firms evaluated in the CIM/DGEHM verification programme. LPG: fixed-price subsidy extended 1 Jun 2026 to 31 May 2027, paid by Hacienda to envasadoras; DGEHM verifying cylinder weight/price (Aug 2026). Pain is low and the buyers are few and larger. Two weak candidates logged.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Coffee law (Ley Especial del Café) reformed Apr 2026: contract reporting to ISC within 10 business days, export permit validity 60 business days, new duty to report third-party coffee intake, processing at other sites needs ISC accreditation, nurseries and seed producers must register. ISC 2025/26 report: 70 beneficiadores, 61 pergamineros, 158 exportadores, 39 torrefactores. Candidate logged. Grain, cocoa and warehouses not searched.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: INSAFOCOOP: Ley General de Asociaciones Cooperativas (1986), art. 70 annual financial statements (2019 circular, current status unverified). No new law found. Cajas de crédito and bancos de los trabajadores: 54 entities, mostly within the FEDECREDITO system and supervised by SSF above a size threshold, so small and well-served. Nothing new beyond a weak INSAFOCOOP idea.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: CSSP found 792 of 1,003 inspected private establishments (78.9%) operating outside the rules between Jun 2025 and May 2026, with 37 temporary closures, 17 of them labs. Reform in force 15 Oct 2025 lets CSSP authorise facilities without the junta de vigilancia favourable report and extends CSSP scope to home medical care and elderly care. Requirements: Conadem accreditation, bio-waste contract, electronic notification authorisation, lab test list. Annual regularisation programme exists. No insurer or state-scheme billing duty checked.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy controlled drugs: known K08, not rechecked. Precursors: Decreto 84 of 1998 (Reglamento de Estupefacientes, Sicotropicos, Precursores) still listed as in force; BCR handles replacement of import/export permits; Superintendencia de Regulacion Sanitaria and CND took part in May 2026 precursor training. Current register and reporting duties for users not confirmed.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security: Ley de los Servicios Privados de Seguridad, registered and controlled by PNC (Division de Registro y Control de Servicios Privados de Seguridad), 30 business-day authorisation. Older reports (InSight Crime, undated in result) say 450+ agencies operated with expired papers and fines were never applied. Date and current numbers unverified. Cleaning and manpower agencies not searched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Quarries and non-metal minerals still under the 1996 Ley de Mineria (licences/concessions via DGEHM). Metallic mining ban repealed: Ley General de Mineria Metalica in force 7 Jan 2025, but it targets large operators. No quarry reporting reform or construction register found. MARN permits under the 1998 Ley del Medio Ambiente, no 2025-26 change found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K01 (AML kit for newly obligated professionals); not rechecked. Related new buyer found in category 32 (digital asset providers).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Ley de Turismo art. 16: special contribution of 5% on accommodation payments (plus $7 air departure). Registro Nacional de Turismo run by Corsatur: one source says 956 firms registered at end of July (year not shown), another says about 160 in 2019 growing 6.4x by 2026. The Reglamento General de la Ley de Turismo requires posted tariffs and safety measures. No guest-register or short-term-rental rule found. Declaration frequency of the 5% not confirmed.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR: El Salvador rated standard risk; dates moved to 30 Dec 2026 (large/medium) and 30 Jun 2027 (micro/small). ISC and ITC run a free Deforestation-Free Trade Gateway portal: 47 exporters in pilot, 282 farms identified, MARN to issue deforestation-free farm certificates, ITC/EU-funded coffee guide. A free portal weakens the case. Cocoa has a traceability registry system (Apr 2025 item). Forced-labour importer declaration is K07, not rechecked. Fish and timber not searched.

coverage.category: 31. Foreign-agent law (RAEX) and non-profit associations with foreign funding
coverage.found: Ley de Agentes Extranjeros approved May 2025: associations and foundations funded or directed by a foreign principal must register with RAEX (Ministerio de Gobernacion) within 90 days, 20 business-day review, 10 days to cure; 30% tax on foreign donations with an exemption for humanitarian or medical work; fines $100,000 to $250,000; one legal opinion says monthly reports to DGII (not confirmed in the official-news text). About 1,000 associations registered with Gobernacion since 2019 (headline only). Politically sensitive; many NGOs may have closed or fled.

coverage.category: 32. Digital asset service providers (Bitcoin and crypto)
coverage.found: Ley de Emision de Activos Digitales (Jan 2023) and later reform adding conduct rules and AML for Bitcoin service providers, supervised by CNAD. 30 entities approved of 120+ applications. Beneficial-owner register and periodic reports to CNAD. Very small buyer group.

coverage.category: 33. Commercial registry duties: CNR matricula renewal and balance deposit for small merchants
coverage.found: CNR matricula de empresa must be renewed every year (fee tied to assets; per branch $34.29 in the source). Sole merchants with assets under $12,000 deposit balances optionally; above that mandatory (undated training slide, unverified). CNR simplified online renewal to 10 steps. Accountants already handle it; no 2026 deadline found.

coverage.category: 34. Occupational safety committees (MTPS) and workplace risk law
coverage.found: Ley General de Prevencion de Riesgos en los Lugares de Trabajo; MTPS reports 1,003 accredited committees (year unknown). No registration platform or new 2026 duty found. MTPS and OEA/RIAL working on a self-assessment form for working conditions (May-Jun 2026).

coverage.category: 35. Coffee nurseries, seed producers and processors at the ISC
coverage.found: Apr 2026 reform: seed producers and nursery operators (semilleristas, viveristas) must now register with ISC, which did not cover them under the March 2024 rules. World Coffee Research sought consultants for a seed and plant traceability system (TNS-MOCCA). Merged into the coffee candidate.

coverage.category: 36. Environmental permits and waste (MARN)
coverage.found: Ley del Medio Ambiente (1998) unchanged for permits; hazardous-waste responsibility lies with the activity owner; $20 fine for littering reform (date unconfirmed). No new register of generators found.

result.competitor: The claim that there is 'no ISC online reporting module' is wrong for the core contract and permit job. Since 12 Aug 2025, BCR, CIEX El Salvador and ISC have run a free, fully digital coffee export permit service. The exporter registers the export sales contract with ISC through an online system, gets pre-authorisation, authorises the operation in SICEX, then draws the permit, guarantee letter and certificate of origin from SFCE. 501 permits were issued from Aug to Dec 2025. BCR is moving export declarations from SICEX to CIEX365 from June 2026. Still open: no ISC portal or private product found for the monthly intermediary report, third-party intake, art. 14 annual reports or nursery registration. The channel ISC uses for these was not verified (isc.gob.sv not opened). Generic coffee traceability SaaS exists, and TechnoServe trained Salvadoran producer groups in traceability software with the old coffee council.
result.duty: Partly confirmed. The Asamblea passed reforms to the Ley Especial para la Comercializacion, Registro y Proteccion de la Propiedad del Cafe on 15 Apr 2026 (El Mundo; elsalvador.com gives 57 votes). The duties it adds: exporters notify ISC of export contracts within 10 business days, and export permits are valid 60 business days and renewable. Intermediaries must keep a register of every coffee sale and report the previous month's operations (receipts, purchases, sales, stock) within the first 10 business days of each month. Beneficiadores, medium and large pergamineros, and torrefactores file an annual art. 14 report within 20 business days of the coffee-year close. Beneficiadores, pergamineros, intermediaries and exporters must report intake of third-party coffee. Semilleristas and viveristas must register with ISC. Processing coffee without ISC accreditation is a serious offence, and buying or selling with an expired registration is a very serious offence. Not found: fine amounts, the Diario Oficial publication or effective date, and the implementing regulation.
result.market: The claim's figures are about 70 beneficiadores, 61 pergamineros, 158 exporters and 39 roasters (ISC 2025/26, per El Mundo; not re-checked). Intermediaries were not counted in the claim and are an extra, likely larger and less digitised group, but no figure was found. The number of nurseries and seed producers is not known. Total market is probably under 500 firms, and the larger exporters likely already have ERP systems.
result.reason: The headline duties, contract reporting and export permits, are already handled by a free state digital channel run by ISC with BCR SFCE, SICEX and CIEX (live since Aug 2025, moving to CIEX365). That knocks out the core of the kit. What remains is uncovered as far as I could tell: monthly intermediary reports, logging third-party coffee intake, the art. 14 annual reports and nursery registration. These form a narrow niche of a few hundred firms, with no fine amounts and no confirmed effective date. Willingness to pay is uncertain because ISC may add its own forms. A possible small pivot is a bookkeeping and monthly-report tool for coffee intermediaries and small beneficios, but the market is very small.

result.competitor: Spanish searches found no software, done-for-you service or gestoría for CSSP/URES authorisation. Clinic and EHR software found is public-sector only (MINSAL SIS, ISSS electronic records). A dedicated gestor search was not run because of budget. No free state self-assessment tool found beyond CSSP's published technical-administrative requirements.
result.duty: Prior CSSP authorisation (certificate of opening and operation) for private non-pharmaceutical health facilities under the Health Code. Reform in force since 15 Oct 2025 (El Mundo, 16 Oct 2025). Requirements: Conadem accreditation, bio-waste disposal contract, e-notification authorisation, lab test list, regency contract, police clearance (owner), fee about $114.29 (CSSP service sheet, 2017). Also an event-driven procedure for replacement, renewal, move, name change or category change. No annual renewal, annual fee or periodic report found (searched 'anualidad'; URES user guide unreachable, HTTP 525). Penalty: temporary closure (37 in Jun 2025 to May 2026) and referral to the Fiscalía; no fine amounts found. Recurrence: not_reached.
result.market: No register total found. Jun 2025 to May 2026: 1,003 private establishments inspected (clinics, pharmacies, labs), 792 (78.9%) irregular, 37 closed. Disciplinary cases by profession: 153 medical, 47 dental, 18 nursing, 17 clinical lab. Small universe, probably low thousands of facilities (estimate, not sourced).
result.reason: The duty is real: private clinics, dental offices and labs need CSSP/URES authorisation. A Health Code reform in the Diario Oficial took effect 15 Oct 2025. It drops the junta's favourable report, adds home-care and elder-care services, and requires Conadem accreditation, a bio-waste contract, e-notification authorisation and a lab test list. The fee is about $114.29 (2017 sheet) and the sanction is closure or referral to the Fiscalía. I found no fixed renewal or periodic filing, so this looks like a one-off duty plus event-driven changes (renewal, move, name change), not a recurring workflow. Search found no software or gestor offering CSSP filing, but that is not proof none exist. Market size is unverified: 1,003 sites inspected and 792 irregular, but no register total.

result.reason: The duty exists. The Ley de los Servicios Privados de Seguridad (2003 decree, still the framework) puts agencies under PNC authorisation and control. The PNC resolves applications in 30 business days after inspecting premises, arms, munitions and personnel files. Fines are 2 to 10 minimum wages (minor) and 11 to 60 (serious). I could not confirm the recurring renewal or reporting content, the regulation's status, or any 2026 enforcement change. InSight Crime (undated) says 450+ agencies had lapsed papers, no agency was ever sanctioned, and a court sided with a fined firm because the regulation was missing. That points to weak enforcement and low willingness to pay. No El Salvador vendor or free state tool was found, but generic guard-management tools (SoftGuard, Guardso, ShiftFlow) exist. The market is small: perhaps a few hundred agencies, and the only count found is 128 agencies in 2006.
